title: Should You Replace Carpet Before Selling a House in Lynnwood?
meta: Replace carpet before selling a Lynnwood house? When new carpet pays off, when cleaning is enough and when to check for oak under it. Wills Flooring explains.
keywords: replace carpet before selling house, new carpet before selling Lynnwood, should I replace carpet or give credit, carpet for selling a house, carpet installation Lynnwood WA

blocks.lead: Replace it if the carpet is stained, matted, smells of pets or is more than about 10 years old. Clean it if it is under five years old and simply dirty. And in a Lynnwood rambler or split-level, lift a corner first, because there is often oak underneath that is worth more than any new carpet.
blocks.detail: New neutral carpet is one of the cheapest changes that transforms listing photos. Wills Flooring brings samples to the house, measures and gives a firm written price at a free estimate, and we tell you honestly if cleaning or refinishing would serve you better.

blocks.html: Every spring we get the same call from Alderwood, Martha Lake and Meadowdale: "We are listing in six weeks, the carpet is tired, do we replace it or just offer a credit?" Lynnwood buyers right now are mostly first-timers and light-rail commuters comparing your house against new townhomes with fresh floors. Tired carpet is the first thing they photograph and the last thing they forget. But replacing it is not always the right move, so here is how we walk sellers through the decision.

blocks.title: Replace, clean, or refinish what is underneath?
blocks.sub: Answer three questions about the carpet you have now.

items.q: How does the carpet look and smell?

opts: Hardwood (or a 1960s to 80s house and you have not checked)

rules.h: Pull it up and look before you spend anything
rules.p: Most Lynnwood ramblers and split-levels from the 1960s to 1980s have oak under the carpet. A refinished original floor outsells new carpet with every buyer we meet. Have us check the wood before you order carpet.

Stains and odor cannot be photographed away, and buyers assume the worst about what is under a stained carpet. A mid-grade neutral carpet with new pad is the fix. Book it before the photographer, not after.

rules.h: Replace it, even if it looks acceptable
rules.p: Carpet over 10 years old has crushed pad and traffic lanes that show in listing photos under bright light. Buyers will price it as a replacement anyway, and they will overestimate the cost when they do.
Carpet under five years old with no damage cleans up well. Have it hot-water extracted a week before photos, restretch any ripples, and spend the carpet money on paint and lighting instead.

default.h: Probably replace the worst rooms only
default.p: Five to ten year old carpet is a judgment call. Replace the stairs, hallway and living room if they show traffic lanes; clean the bedrooms if they are intact. Mixing is fine as long as the colors read as intentional.

blocks.text: What Lynnwood buyers are comparing you against

items.title: New townhomes near the light rail
items.text: Much of the Lynnwood buyer pool has just toured new construction around the City Center station with vinyl plank main floors and fresh carpet upstairs. Your 1978 split-level does not need to match that, but 15-year-old beige carpet next to it looks like work.

items.title: First-time buyers with no cash left
items.text: After a down payment and closing costs, most Lynnwood first-timers have no budget for floors. A house that needs carpet on day one gets mentally discounted by more than the carpet costs. That gap is the whole argument for replacing before listing.

items.title: Inspectors and pet odor
items.text: Pet urine soaks into pad and subfloor. New carpet over a contaminated pad still smells in August. If a dog lived on it, the pad must go and the subfloor may need sealing, which is a detail buyers' inspectors specifically sniff for.

items.title: The oak underneath
items.text: Alderwood and Meadowdale ramblers from the 1960s and 70s were built with oak strip floors and carpeted over in the 1990s. Refinished oak is the single most requested feature in local listings. Check before you buy carpet.

blocks.text: Which carpet to buy when you are selling

items.html: Mid-grade, not premium. Buyers cannot tell a 40 oz nylon from a 60 oz one in a showing. They can tell new from old. Spend on the pad and the color, not the top tier.
Polyester or triexta texture, short pile. Both are stain-resistant, come in the right neutrals and photograph cleanly. A short textured pile hides footprints and vacuum lines during showings.
Warm greige or light taupe. Not white, which shows every showing. Not dark, which shrinks a 1970s bedroom. Ask to see the sample against your wall paint in daylight.
A 6 to 8 lb rebond pad. New pad is most of why new carpet feels new underfoot. This is the one place we push sellers not to go cheap.
Do the stairs and hallway first. If budget is tight, the stairs and upper hall are what every buyer touches. Bedrooms can follow in the same color if cash allows.

blocks.title: The expensive one:
blocks.text: Ordering carpet before anyone checks what is under it. We have pulled up brand-new carpet in Martha Lake to find clean oak that could have been refinished for the listing. Lift a corner in a closet, or have us look at the free estimate before you commit.

items: Replacing only one bedroom in a slightly different color. Buyers notice the mismatch and assume the rest is next.
Installing new carpet over the old pad to save a little. Odor and crushed spots come straight through.
Scheduling install after the photographer. The photos are the listing; the carpet has to be in before the camera.
Choosing a trendy pattern or a bold color. You are decorating for the widest possible buyer, not for yourself.
Waiting until the week before listing. Order to install is usually one to two weeks, and spring in Lynnwood books up fast.

faq.q: Does new carpet increase the sale price of a house in Lynnwood?
faq.a: It rarely adds more than it costs on paper, but it removes a reason for buyers to discount or walk. In Lynnwood, where most buyers are first-timers comparing against new townhomes, a house that needs carpet gets mentally marked down by more than a carpet job costs. New carpet protects the price rather than inflating it.

faq.q: Is it better to replace the carpet or give the buyer a credit?
faq.a: Replace it, in most cases. Buyers overestimate what carpet costs, so a credit almost always ends up larger than the actual job. Credits can also be capped by the buyer's lender. A credit only makes sense if you are out of time or selling to an investor who plans to remodel.

faq.q: How do I know if there is hardwood under my carpet?
faq.a: Pull back a corner in a closet or near a floor vent. Lynnwood ramblers and split-levels built from the 1960s through the early 1980s very often have oak strip flooring under the carpet. If you find wood, have us check its condition before spending anything on new carpet.

faq.q: What color carpet sells a house best?
faq.a: A warm greige or light taupe in a short textured pile. It photographs as clean and neutral, works with most wall colors, and hides footprints during showings. Avoid very light carpet that shows every visitor and dark carpet that makes 1970s bedrooms feel smaller than they are.

faq.q: How long before listing should I schedule carpet installation?
faq.a: Book the estimate about six weeks before your listing date. Ordering usually takes one to two weeks and installation takes one to two days, which leaves time for paint touch-ups and photos. Spring is the busiest season in Lynnwood, so add a week of margin if you are listing in April or May.

faq.q: Can I just replace the carpet in the worst rooms?
faq.a: Yes, as long as the new and old carpets are clearly separated by a doorway or a stair and the colors read as intentional. Stairs, upper hallway and living room show wear first and matter most in showings. Bedrooms with intact carpet can be professionally cleaned instead.
